LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources the PKGBUILD and executes its global/top-level scope. In this file, that scope consists entirely of package metadata variables, dependency arrays, a `source` array pointing to the official Tibia download URLs, `sha256sums` with `SKIP`, and a `DLAGENTS` array assignment that configures `curl` for HTTPS downloads with a referer header.

There are no top-level command substitutions, no external commands invoked at parse time, no network requests, no downloads, and no data exfiltration. The `prepare()` and `package()` functions are not executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so their contents are outside the scope of this gate. The `SKIP` checksums are irrelevant at this step because no sources are downloaded or verified during `--printsrcinfo`. The custom `DLAGENTS` entry is a normal makepkg mechanism for fetching the package's own declared upstream source, not malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Global scope is benign; no code executes at parse time. SAFE.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Global scope is benign; no code executes at parse time. SAFE.
Note: 2 remote source(s) have no checksum (sha256sums=SKIP), so the bytes are not verifiable: tibia.tar.gz::https://static.tibia.com/download/tibia.x64.tar.gz, tibia-agreement.php::https://www.tibia.com/support/agreement.php

<details>
This is a standard `.gitignore` file for an AUR package repository. It excludes common build/package directories (`pkg/`, `src/`), a generated license/download file (`agreement.php`), and builds of the `tibia` binary, while explicitly allowing patch files to remain tracked. There are no network requests, no code execution, no obfuscation, and no file manipulation outside the normal packaging workflow. Nothing in this file presents a security concern.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard .gitignore for AUR package; no malicious behavior found.</summary>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD downloads the official Tibia game binary from `https://static.tibia.com/download/tibia.x64.tar.gz` (over HTTPS) and the license agreement from `https://www.tibia.com/support/agreement.php`. All network operations target the project's own domain (tibia.com) and use HTTPS.  

The prepare step runs `html2text` on the downloaded agreement PHP page to produce a plain‑text LICENSE file – this is simply converting the HTML license to text, not executing any code from the page. The package step copies the unpacked game to `/opt/tibia`, creates a symlink in `/usr/bin`, and installs a desktop entry, icon, and license file into standard locations.  

No obfuscation, suspicious commands (eval, curl|bash, base64), backdoors, data exfiltration, or operations outside the application's own scope are present. The SHA‑256 sums are set to `SKIP`, which is a trust/hygiene choice rather than evidence of malice. The script follows normal AUR packaging patterns for a binary redistribution package.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR binary package, no malicious indicators.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This `.SRCINFO` file is a standard metadata file for an Arch User Repository (AUR) package. It declares the package name (`tibia`), description, upstream URL, dependencies, and two source files: the official binary tarball from `static.tibia.com` and an agreement page from `tibia.com`. Both URLs point to the official Tibia website, which is expected for this game package. The checksums are set to `SKIP`—this is common for binary downloads and VCS sources and is not, by itself, evidence of malice. No executable scripts or suspicious operations are present; the file only contains declarative metadata.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>AUR metadata file, no executable content, safe.</summary>
</security_assessment>

The `source` array contains only direct HTTPS URLs pointing to the official Tibia game download and agreement page, which is expected for this package. The `DLAGENTS` override is limited to modifying curl behavior for HTTPS downloads, using standard and safe options (e.g., `--compressed`, `-fLC -`, `-e %u`), and does not introduce any code execution or data exfiltration mechanisms. There are no command substitutions, evals, or function calls at the global scope that would be triggered during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no immediate risk.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package for the Tibia game, a legitimate online game distributed by CipSoft. It fetches a prebuilt binary from the official and expected source (`static.tibia.com`) using a direct HTTPS URL. The use of `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is not inherently unsafe, as it is common practice for VCS or binary-only packages where reproducibility is not feasible, and the source domain matches the official game domain.

The build process uses standard, safe operations: `gendesk` generates a desktop entry, `html2text` converts the license agreement to plain text, and files are installed into appropriate directories under `$pkgdir`. The binary is placed in `/opt`, with a symlink in `/usr/bin`, which is conventional for such packages. No obfuscated code, suspicious network activity, or unauthorized system modifications are present.

All dependencies are legitimate libraries required for GUI and multimedia functionality, and the maintainer-provided scripts (e.g., `prepare()` and `package()`) perform only expected packaging tasks. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or supply-chain compromise.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard, safe packaging of official game binary
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided <.SRCINFO> file is metadata for the Arch User Repository (AUR) package `tibia` and does not contain executable code. It declares the package's source URLs, dependencies, and checksums. The sources point to the official Cipsoft-hosted Tibia game binary (`tibia.x64.tar.gz`) and the game's user agreement, both over HTTPS from domains owned by the game's developer. This is consistent with standard packaging practices for official prebuilt binaries.

The `sha256sums = SKIP` entries are expected for VCS or dynamically fetched binaries where reproducibility cannot be guaranteed, and while they reduce verifiability, they do not constitute malicious behavior. The AUR allows `SKIP` for such cases, especially when packaging official binaries that may change between versions. No network requests, file modifications, or executable logic are embedded in this file. The dependencies and optional dependencies are standard system libraries and Qt6 components required for GUI and multimedia functionality, typical for a game client.

There is no evidence of obfuscated code, unauthorized network activity, or system modifications. The file adheres to standard AUR metadata conventions and poses no security threat.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Metadata-only file with expected SKIP checksums; no malicious content
</summary>
</security_assessment>
